q: Which hormone, nicknamed the 'cuddle hormone', surges during orgasm and breastfeeding?
note: It also helps trigger contractions during labour.

q: Which human organ is widely described as the only one whose sole purpose is pleasure?
note: Most of it lies inside the body; the visible part is only the tip.

q: What is the correct term for the external female genitals as a whole?
note: The vagina is only the internal canal; people mix them up constantly.

q: In the contraceptive 'IUD', what does the 'I' stand for?
note: Some copper versions are licensed to stay in for up to 10 years.

q: Under good conditions, how long can sperm survive inside the female reproductive tract?
note: That's why sex days before ovulation can still lead to pregnancy.

q: How long does an egg typically survive after ovulation if it isn't fertilised?
note: Usually just one egg is released per cycle.

q: What does the abbreviation STI stand for?
note: Many clinics prefer it to 'STD' because infections often have no symptoms.

q: Which vaccine protects against the virus behind most cervical cancers and genital warts?
note: Serum Institute's Cervavac is India's first indigenous version.

q: Which bacterial STI, once called 'the great pox', is still treated with penicillin?
note: Named after a shepherd in a 1530 Italian poem by Girolamo Fracastoro.

q: What does PrEP, a medicine HIV-negative people take to stay negative, stand for?
note: Its cousin PEP is a month-long course taken after a possible exposure.

q: In the HIV campaign slogan 'U=U', 'Undetectable' equals what?
note: Effective treatment means HIV cannot be passed on through sex.

q: Can someone get pregnant the very first time they have sex?
note: Sperm meeting an egg doesn't care whether it's the first time or the fiftieth.

q: Kegel exercises are designed to strengthen which muscles?
note: Named after gynaecologist Arnold Kegel, who described them in 1948.

q: After ejaculation, the recovery time before another erection or orgasm is possible is called the what?
note: It usually gets longer with age.

q: Sildenafil, the drug in Viagra, was first trialled as a treatment for which chest-pain heart condition?
note: Trial volunteers reported a rather unexpected side effect.

q: Where in the body is the prostate gland located?
note: Doctors can feel it through the rectal wall during a check-up.

q: Why do the testicles hang outside the body in the scrotum?
a: To stay cooler for sperm production
options: To stay cooler for sperm production
note: Sperm production works best a few degrees below core body temperature.

q: Which muscle pulls the testicles closer to the body when it's cold?
note: Stroking the inner thigh can also trigger it, a reflex doctors test.

q: Which pair of glands beside the vaginal opening secretes some lubricating fluid during arousal?
note: Most lubrication actually seeps through the vaginal walls as blood flow increases.

q: Pre-ejaculate, or 'pre-cum', is produced mainly by which glands?
note: It can pick up sperm, so pulling out is far from foolproof.

q: Out of 100 couples relying only on the pull-out method for a year, roughly how many get pregnant with typical use?
note: Timing it perfectly every single time is much harder than people think.

q: What is the minor surgery that cuts or seals the sperm-carrying tubes as permanent male contraception?
note: Semen still comes out afterwards; it just contains no sperm.

q: What is the common name for female sterilisation that blocks or cuts the oviducts?
note: India's family planning programme usually calls it tubectomy.

q: When should an emergency contraceptive pill be taken for it to work best?
note: It works mainly by delaying ovulation; it is not an abortion pill.

q: India's well-known emergency contraceptive pill brand is called 'Unwanted' followed by which number?
note: The number nods to the window, in hours, after unprotected sex.

q: Which contraceptive is a matchstick-sized rod placed under the skin of the upper arm?
note: It lasts up to 3 years and is over 99% effective.

q: How often is the contraceptive injection (DMPA) typically given?
note: India offers it free in government facilities under the name Antara.

q: Chhaya (centchroman), India's hormone-free weekly contraceptive pill, was developed by which institute?
note: It's taken twice weekly for the first three months, then weekly.

q: The 'mini-pill' contains only one type of hormone. Which one?
note: The combined pill adds an oestrogen to the mix.

q: A surge of which hormone triggers ovulation?
note: Home ovulation kits work by detecting this surge in urine.

q: Home pregnancy tests detect which hormone in urine?
note: It starts being made soon after a fertilised egg attaches to the womb lining.

q: In a textbook 28-day menstrual cycle, ovulation happens around which day?
note: Real cycles vary a lot, which makes calendar counting unreliable.

q: What is the medical term for a person's very first period?
note: Mittelschmerz, by the way, is German for 'middle pain' at ovulation.

q: Which French phrase for orgasm literally means 'the little death'?
note: It refers to the brief blissful fade afterwards, nothing grim.

q: What is the name for a painful erection lasting over four hours, which is a medical emergency?
note: Named after Priapus, a Greek fertility god.

q: What is the term for involuntary tightening of the vaginal muscles that makes penetration painful or impossible?
note: It's very treatable, often with physiotherapy, vaginal trainers and counselling.

q: What is the everyday name for vaginal candidiasis, a very common infection that isn't an STI?
note: Antibiotics, tight synthetic underwear and douching can all encourage it.

q: Peeing soon after sex is commonly recommended to help reduce the risk of what?
note: It flushes bacteria from the urethra, but it won't prevent pregnancy.

q: Which of these cannot transmit HIV?
note: Hugs, sweat, toilet seats and mosquitoes don't spread it either.

q: HIV attacks which type of white blood cell, whose count doctors track?
note: Modern treatment lets the count recover to healthy levels.

q: Which bacterial STI is nicknamed 'the clap'?
note: WHO warns some strains are becoming resistant to antibiotics.

q: Cold sores and many genital sores are caused by which virus?
note: Most people who carry it have no symptoms and don't know.

q: Which tiny parasites, nicknamed 'crabs', can be passed on through close intimate contact?
note: Their scientific name is Pthirus pubis.

q: Trichomoniasis, a common STI, is caused by what kind of organism?
note: WHO counts it among the most common curable STIs worldwide.

q: What is the medical term for semen containing no sperm at all?
note: It's often treatable, and sperm can sometimes still be retrieved surgically.

q: Which of these infections, which can spread through sex, is prevented by a routine vaccine?
note: India's Universal Immunisation Programme includes it; it spreads through blood and body fluids.

q: In Planned Parenthood's FRIES model of consent, what does the 'S' stand for?
note: A yes to one thing is not a yes to everything else.

q: What is the consent standard called where a clear, active 'yes' is needed, not just the absence of a 'no'?
note: Silence or no response never counts as agreement.

q: A famous 2015 UK consent video compares sex to offering someone which hot drink?
note: Its lesson: if they don't want it, don't make them drink it.

q: Male and female external genitals develop from the same embryonic bump. What is it called?
note: For roughly the first two months, all embryos look the same down there.

q: Which much-debated erogenous zone on the front vaginal wall is named after a German gynaecologist's initial?
note: Ernst Gräfenberg described the area in 1950; the catchy name came in 1981.

q: What mainly causes an erection?
note: Healthy men get several erections a night during REM sleep.

q: What is the name of the bone found in the penis of many mammals, but not humans?
note: Most primates, including chimpanzees, have a small one.

q: What is the formal medical term for a 'wet dream'?
note: They can happen with or without a dream you remember.

q: Anxiety that losing semen drains strength is described in South Asia as which culture-bound syndrome?
note: Semen is constantly produced; releasing it causes no weakness at all.

q: Does masturbation cause blindness, acne or physical weakness?
note: Doctors agree it's a normal, healthy part of sexuality.

q: Which screening test checks the cervix for changes that could lead to cancer?
note: Named after Greek doctor Georgios Papanikolaou.

q: Where does fertilisation of an egg normally take place?
note: The embryo then travels to the womb, settling into its lining about a week later.

q: By volume, which is the largest cell in the human body?
note: About 0.1 mm across, it's just about visible to the naked eye.

q: Which sex chromosome must the sperm carry for a baby to be genetically male?
note: The egg always contributes an X.

q: Erection is mainly parasympathetic. Emission, the first stage of ejaculation, is driven by which nervous system?
note: Medical students remember it as 'Point and Shoot'.

q: What does the 'orgasm gap' refer to?
a: Straight women orgasm less than straight men
options: Straight women orgasm less than straight men
note: A 2018 US study found lesbian women orgasm more often than straight women.

q: In LGBTQIA+, what does the 'A' most commonly stand for?
note: It describes people who feel little or no sexual attraction; 'ace' for short.

q: What term describes someone who feels sexual attraction only after a strong emotional bond forms?
note: It sits under the broader 'ace' spectrum umbrella.

q: Which Latin-derived word, popularised by Freud, means sex drive?
note: It naturally rises and falls with stress, sleep and hormones.

q: Which hormone released after orgasm is linked to that satisfied, sleepy feeling?
note: One study found a bigger rise after partnered sex than after solo play.

q: In HIV, what does the 'I' stand for?
note: It's a virus; AIDS is the late stage that treatment now usually prevents.

q: 'Spanish fly', long sold as a supposed sex booster, is actually made from what?
note: Its active chemical, cantharidin, is toxic and can seriously damage the urinary tract.

q: Which condom material is a common option for people with latex allergies?
note: Polyisoprene is another latex-free option.

q: Which type of lubricant should not be used with latex condoms?
note: Oil weakens latex, so coconut oil and condoms don't mix.

q: What does wearing two condoms at once ('double-bagging') do to protection?
note: Always check the expiry date too; old latex tears more easily.

q: In STI testing, what is the 'window period'?
a: Time before a test can detect infection
options: Days an opened condom stays usable
Time before a test can detect infection
note: That's why clinics sometimes ask you to retest a few weeks later.

q: Where is the perineum?
note: Its cheeky slang names include 'taint' and 'gooch'.

q: What are the small glands near the urethra, nicknamed the 'female prostate', usually called?
note: Small studies suggest squirting fluid comes mostly from the bladder, with a little from these glands.

q: What is the medical term for persistent pain during or after sex?
note: It's common and treatable, so it's worth raising with a doctor.

q: Which condition sees tissue similar to the womb lining grow elsewhere, often causing painful periods and sex?
note: WHO estimates it affects roughly 1 in 10 women of reproductive age.

q: In PCOS, a common hormonal condition, what does the 'O' stand for?
note: Despite the name, the 'cysts' are really immature follicles.

q: Which is the most effective form of emergency contraception?
note: It can be fitted up to five days after unprotected sex.

q: Which of these is a myth, not a real method of contraception?
note: Sperm can reach the cervix within minutes; no rinse is faster.

q: What does 'LARC' stand for in contraception?
note: Most are 'fit and forget' methods that last for years once in.

q: 'Blue balls' is informally given which medical-sounding name?
note: It fades on its own and never requires sex to relieve it.

q: Men are advised to regularly self-check their testicles to catch which cancer early?
note: It's one of the most curable cancers when caught early.

q: Which bacteria mainly keep the vagina healthy and slightly acidic?
note: It's self-cleaning, which is why doctors say douching does more harm than good.

q: Which thin membrane at the vaginal opening is wrongly believed to prove virginity?
note: It varies hugely and can stretch naturally; WHO calls virginity testing unscientific.

q: What is the medical term for difficulty reaching orgasm despite enough stimulation?
note: It's common and often improves with communication, time and less pressure.

q: Alongside 'stop-start', which classic self-help method is used for premature ejaculation?
note: Premature ejaculation is very common and usually very treatable.

q: In men's health, what does 'ED' stand for?
note: It can be an early warning sign of heart disease, so it's worth checking.

q: What are the inner and outer skin folds around the vaginal opening called?
note: Latin for 'lips'; they come in hugely varied shapes, all normal.

q: Venereology, the medical study of STIs, is named after which Roman goddess of love?
note: Indian skin specialists often train in it under the 'DVL' degree.

q: What is the nickname for the reddish rash that can spread across the chest during arousal and orgasm?
note: It's caused by blood vessels widening and fades soon after.

q: Mpox, renamed by WHO in 2022, spreads mainly through what?
note: Its old name came from its 1958 discovery in lab monkeys.

q: What is the thin latex square used as a barrier for safer oral sex called?
note: No dam handy? A condom cut open lengthwise does the job.

q: On the combined pill, the monthly bleed during the pill-free week is actually what?
options: A side effect of missed pills
note: UK guidance says skipping the break is safe for most users.

q: Tracking body temperature and cervical mucus to avoid or plan pregnancy is called what?
note: It needs careful daily tracking, so typical-use failure rates are much higher.

q: Which 'reward' brain chemical rises with sexual anticipation and desire?
note: It's the same chemical behind cravings for food, games and endless scrolling.

q: In retrograde ejaculation, where does semen go instead of out of the body?
note: It's often linked to certain medicines, prostate surgery or diabetes.

q: Does taking the Pill for years make it hard to get pregnant later?
options: Yes, for at least a decade
note: Fertility usually returns quickly after stopping hormonal contraception.

q: Mala-D and Mala-N are Indian government brands of which contraceptive?
note: The government hands them out free or at subsidised prices.

q: How often is a contraceptive skin patch usually changed?
note: Three weekly patches are followed by a patch-free week, or no break at all.
